1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Record
88	   **claim or literal criterion; source and locator; current authority/status;
89	   change actually authorized; actual operation prerequisite; finding and
90	   disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted, not just the specialist's
91	   statement that a source supports it. Split mixed-authority clauses. If a
92	   rule rejects a plausible alternative, explain whether the source excludes
93	   that alternative or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve
94	   required outcomes when correcting an unsupported recipe.
95	
96	3. For each requested answer, assume only that answer is supplied and trace
97	   the exact state/contract changes and next available operation. Each other
98	   choice keeps its status unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited
99	   existing decision already establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in
100	   the question, decision table and proposed operation; matching current values
101	   does not prove that a proposed status change is authorized. Check actual
102	   runtime/tool prerequisites and name the dependencies that remain. Scoped
103	   expert proposals can support an authorized sample; do not turn every proposal
104	   into a new owner-confirmation requirement or treat later production
105	   prerequisites as blockers for independent local work.
106	
107	4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
108	   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
109	   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
110	   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
111	   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
112	   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
113	   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.
114	
115	5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
116	   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
117	   affected claims against the sources. Bind your adoption finding to that final
118	   version; a clean summary cannot override contradictory saved criteria or
119	   continuation instructions. Finish with useful saved progress, any still
120	   necessary direct question to the owner, and the concrete operation its answer
121	   enables. Carry existing authorization and leave later prerequisites explicit.
122	
123	## Specialist → caller at completion
124	
125	Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
126	PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
127	of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
128	from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
129	without manufacturing PLAR or production records:
130	
131	- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
132	- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
133	- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
134	- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
135	- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
136	- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
137	- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.
138	
139	When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.
140	
141	Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.
142	
143	Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.
144	
145	The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.
146	
147	For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
148	use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
149	`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
150	selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
151	CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
152	--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
153	complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
154	Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
155	file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
156	keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
157	saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
158	Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
159	Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
160	requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
161	active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
162	when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.
163	
164	`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
165	expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
166	caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
167	`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
168	runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
169	The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
170	does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.
171	
172	Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
173	and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
174	[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
175	in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
176	contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
177	confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
178	judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
179	these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
180	A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
181	not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
182	`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
183	not automatically summarized.
184	
185	For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:
186	
187	```json
188	{
189	  "status": "partial",
190	  "caller": {
191	    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
192	    "integration": {
193	      "status": "not_performed",
194	      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
195	    },
196	    "issues": [
197	      {
198	        "category": "unfinished_work",
199	        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
200	        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
201	      }
202	    ]
203	  }
204	}
205	```
206	
207	Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
208	to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
209	hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
210	JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
211	Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
212	`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.
213	
214	Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
215	Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
216	JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
217	truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
218	pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
219	These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
220	after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
221	recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
222	criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.
223	
224	On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
225	requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
226	its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
227	actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
228	explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.
229	
230	Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.
231

caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
changing the user's global configuration.

A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.

## Specialist → caller while working

Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.

Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.

Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.

Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.

## Caller: review a cold continuation

A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.

1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
   authority for the next work.

2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Record
   **claim or literal criterion; source and locator; current authority/status;
   change actually authorized; actual operation prerequisite; finding and
   disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted, not just the specialist's
   statement that a source supports it. Split mixed-authority clauses. If a
   rule rejects a plausible alternative, explain whether the source excludes
   that alternative or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve
   required outcomes when correcting an unsupported recipe.

3. For each requested answer, assume only that answer is supplied and trace
   the exact state/contract changes and next available operation. Each other
   choice keeps its status unless the answer explicitly adopts it or a cited
   existing decision already establishes it. Compare every claimed effect in
   the question, decision table and proposed operation; matching current values
   does not prove that a proposed status change is authorized. Check actual
   runtime/tool prerequisites and name the dependencies that remain. Scoped
   expert proposals can support an authorized sample; do not turn every proposal
   into a new owner-confirmation requirement or treat later production
   prerequisites as blockers for independent local work.

4. When this comparison finds a discrepancy, send your own precise finding and
   source evidence to the same native specialist. Ask for a corrected current
   proposal with an explicit old-to-new explanation, preserving the historical
   artifacts and acceptance. Wait for the revision. If the first return is
   consistent, record the independent comparison without inventing a correction
   round. Do not declare consistency solely because the specialist followed a
   checklist, retained earlier bytes or returned a valid state.

5. After the last specialist change, reopen the actual final files and current
   state, verify their identities and applicable runtime checks, and recheck the
   affected claims against the sources. Bind your adoption finding to that final
   version; a clean summary cannot override contradictory saved criteria or
   continuation instructions. Finish with useful saved progress, any still
   necessary direct question to the owner, and the concrete operation its answer
   enables. Carry existing authorization and leave later prerequisites explicit.

## Specialist → caller at completion

Return a compact structured result (JSON or equivalent named fields). For a
PLAR-bound assignment, use the [caller view](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md)
of the existing handoff operation so production identities and continuation come
from saved state. Direct briefs and planning-only work can use the fields below
without manufacturing PLAR or production records:

- `status`: `delivered`, `partial`, `needs_input`, or `blocked`, judged against this assignment.
- `asset_id` and `requirements_hash` when PLAR supplied them; direct-brief tasks identify their brief.
- `artifacts`: project-relative paths, role, actual hashes and dimensions/frame metadata as relevant.
- `checks`: actual mechanical, visual and integration findings, with evidence paths and unavailable checks.
- `request_review`: packet and caller-review paths/hashes, with unresolved findings when applicable.
- `provider`: observed resource/job IDs and the production-state location needed to resume.
- `questions` or `next`: only outstanding decisions and the next concrete action.

When durable production state is in use, finish its accepted-candidate selection and task state through `task-complete` / `pixl_task_complete` after the saved required checks pass. The caller reads `workflow` to confirm the completed state agrees with the delivered files; an open task remains an explicit unfinished part of the operation. A planning-only assignment does not need manufactured production state.

Judge completion against the delegated scope. A planning-only assignment is delivered when its complete reviewed contract is returned; future generation remains outside that scope. An assignment ending at an accepted request is delivered when that request and its resumable state are returned, while the asset remains unaccepted and its production task open. State both facts explicitly. A full asset-production assignment is still partial at contract handoff. Retain the provider connection and simulated/live provenance with every job ID and next action; an ID cannot be resumed on a different service.

Include only applicable fields. A generation-only task can deliver a reviewed artifact while explicitly leaving engine import unverified. If the assignment requires integration, unavailable integration keeps that part unfinished. Never use a provider's completed status as artistic acceptance.

The caller opens the returned files and checks the relevant result against its original assignment. Compare a fresh selected PLAR packet if source context changed. `requirements_hash` tracks the selected requirements, reference bytes and dependency requirements; status/next-action changes alone do not change it. It is neither a spend authorization nor a readiness verdict. The existing file `hash` still governs PLAR writes.

For a PLAR-bound result, reread the selected asset after the last state change, then
use `pixl_plar_handoff` with its `asset_id`, `requirements_hash`,
`production.continuation.state_hash` as `expect`, and your `details` object. The
selected read's top-level `hash` identifies the PLAR file, not production state.
CLI: `plar handoff DETAILS_JSON --path QUEUE --asset ID
--requirements HASH --expect STATE_HASH --view caller --root PROJECT`. The operation saves the
complete derived continuation and immediate `next` unchanged in an immutable file.
Return the caller view and its exact handoff locator; the caller opens the retained
file and compares its state identity with fresh focused PLAR. Omitting `--view caller`
keeps the existing receipt response. The view does not add acceptance or alter the
saved handoff. Do not copy selected fields into a rewritten resume.
Older handoffs remain readable; their original bytes are not migrated or relabelled.
Before returning a reviewed open task, check its current nominee and workflow
requirements. Saved verdicts on an unselected candidate do not describe the
active output. Nominate the intended candidate through normal state authoring
when appropriate; preserve unavailable verdicts and leave the task open.

`details` contains your assignment status, delivered artifacts, request-review links,
expert reasoning, actual checks, unresolved issues and future work. Keep completed
caller actions with evidence in `details.caller_actions`, and subsequent goals in
`details.future_work`. A completed caller review can be reported there while the
runtime still derives `review_delivery`; it does not replace that derived action.
The snapshot records both facts without inventing a new acceptance event. The runtime
does not decide whether your artistic judgment or assignment-status claim is correct.

Use optional `details.caller` for the bounded ordinary return: summary, artifact
and report locators, issues and integration findings, following its closed
[contract](../../../resources/spec/caller-result.md). Retain complete observations
in the other details fields and referenced files. Each declared file reference
contains exactly `path`, `sha256` and `role`; the runtime verifies its current
confined file bytes before publishing. These checks do not verify the role or
judgment you supplied. The caller view distinguishes
these authored claims from derived task, acceptance and continuation facts.
A missing integration observation stays unreported; an accepted candidate does
not manufacture an assignment-status or integration claim. Without `details.caller`,
`caller.present` is false and the full details remain retrievable; legacy prose is
not automatically summarized.

For example, only when the assigned destination inspection remains unperformed:

```json
{
  "status": "partial",
  "caller": {
    "summary": "Candidate bytes are retained; required destination inspection remains unperformed.",
    "integration": {
      "status": "not_performed",
      "summary": "No destination observation has been made for this assignment."
    },
    "issues": [
      {
        "category": "unfinished_work",
        "summary": "The assigned destination check has not run.",
        "recovery": "Run the assigned destination check, retain its actual evidence and refresh the handoff."
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Use actual findings and omit inapplicable fields. Summary/recovery text is bounded
to 600 characters; artifact, report, issue and integration-evidence arrays each
hold at most 12 entries, and the complete caller block at most 8192 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes. Move detail to linked files instead of truncating obligations.
Integration status is `pass`, `fail`, `unavailable`, `not_performed` or
`not_in_scope`; omission is not one of those observations.

Follow the returned full-handoff, details and resume locators for exact retrieval.
Read `resume_inline`: the unchanged `resume` is present up to 4096 compact UTF-8
JSON bytes; otherwise `resume_ref` retrieves it in full. It is never rewritten or
truncated. `details_ref` and `resume_ref` identify physical source ranges and JSON
pointers in the same immutable handoff. Use its `path`/`sha256` for the full file.
These facts describe the captured selection; use the returned `refresh` read
after source or state changes, and reconcile the current identities. Read that full resume before acting on its jobs or
recovery instructions. Keep routine responses useful without pasting the complete
criteria audit, request report or tool transcript into the return.

On a cold resume, read the saved handoff and current focused PLAR. Changed state or
requirements require a fresh snapshot; matching hashes preserve the original job and
its originating connection. Resolve pending work, then retrieve/import and review its
actual result before proposing another generation. The caller's normal response can
explain later work in prose while linking the exact resumable artifact.

Keep detailed receipts in project files so the caller receives useful art and decisions rather than an entire transcript or image encoded in text.

1	---
2	name: pixl
3	description: "Delegate PixelLab visual asset work: UI icons and panels, pixel fonts, coherent characters, animation, tiles, reference matching, inspection and project integration. Developing PIXL's profile, skills, runtime or packaging is a maintainer task and does not activate this profile."
4	model: inherit
5	---
6	
7	When activated for pixel-art production, you are PIXL, the pixel-art production expert. A maintainer reading this definition to develop or review the project keeps the development role. When skill invocation is available, load `pixl:pixl` to obtain the canonical instructions and installed skill location. Read `skills/pixl/SKILL.md` and `resources/agent/PROFILE.md` from this plugin's root before production work. Resolve that root from the skill's reported location or this agent definition's installed path: it is the parent of this file's `agents` directory. Read linked references relative to the file containing the link. If the harness does not expose either location, use its plugin inventory; do not guess from the current project directory.
8	
9	## When to invoke
10	
11	- Produce or extend coherent UI assets, fonts, characters, animation, tiles, environments, or modular pixel-art assets.
12	- Review native-scale readability, source-specific style, animation continuity, tile joins, or engine import behavior.
13	- Plan and operate actual PixelLab tools while preserving evidence and validated PIXL UDL state.
14	
15	Establish the user's references and project contract, choose and research methods, and prove uncertain methods with a representative artifact. Inherit the host's model and available tools; inspect actual tool schemas before calling them. The local PIXL runtime manages state and evidence. Submit and poll real generation only through the separately authenticated PixelLab service, preserving its returned IDs. Local preparation and journal changes are not remote execution.
16	
17	Inspect produced images mechanically and visually; verify import behavior where required. Respect the project's own palette, edge treatment, animation, and rendering decisions. Report delivered artifacts, observed job states, verification evidence, and unresolved limitations. Keep mutable work under the chosen project root and commit production state only with its current expected hash.
18	
19	For source-code asset allocation, load the PLAR skill and pass the consumer root and selected asset ID into production. Include UI states, icons, panels and project assets when they are actual consumers. A delegated task needs the brief, references, constraints and authorization explicitly; do not assume the parent's conversation was inherited.
20	
21	Use the common skill's delegation and PixelLab-operation references. Receive the caller's requirements and reference roles, ask the caller only consequential unresolved questions, and return actual files, checks, provider/state IDs and the next action. Select from the official PixelLab tool surface by the deliverable and supported visual inputs.
22

1	# Agent-to-agent asset work
2	
3	Use this operation when a calling Claude/Codex agent assigns visual work to PIXL. PIXL is the callable name of pixel-lab-agent (PLA). The profile supplies artistic judgment; this contract carries the assignment and result between agents.
4	
5	## Caller → specialist
6	
7	Supply the smallest complete assignment:
8	
9	| Context | What the specialist needs |
10	| --- | --- |
11	| Outcome | Asset purpose, requested files and relevant success criteria |
12	| Workspace | Absolute consumer root; installed PIXL skill location |
13	| Requirements | Selected PLAR asset packet, or a complete direct brief |
14	| References | Addressable files/owned resource IDs, their roles and what to preserve |
15	| Authority | User decisions, proposals, unresolved choices and established authorization/limits |
16	| Resume | Existing store/task/output and pending provider IDs, when present |
17	| Integration | Destination, relevant consumers, and authorized code/import work |
18	
19	Keep generated assets, request/review artifacts, helper scripts and scratch/previews inside the assigned consumer root unless the assignment names another authorized destination. Resolve paths against that root through each delegation and resumption; the shell's current directory or the kit's installation directory is not an implicit output destination. The caller checks returned paths against the agreed workspace as well as checking their bytes.
20	
21	For PLAR, call `pixl_plar_read` with `asset_id`. Pass its selected row, transitive dependencies, source bindings, visual references and `requirements_hash`. Queue summaries alone omit production context. The reader supplies absolute paths for this filesystem; if the delegate uses another workspace, rebase paths and verify the same source bytes there.
22	
23	The caller delegates to the native PIXL agent or a native specialist loading the shared PIXL skill. Keep the caller's model/tool/permission settings unless the assignment requires otherwise. Include the actual assignment in the delegation; naming a skill or saying “make the assets” does not transfer the parent's conversation. Credentials stay in the host's PixelLab connection.
24	
25	When the assignment is to reassess or correct retained work, separate two scopes in
26	the delegation. **Historical evidence stays unchanged:** the original request, plan,
27	criteria, candidate, verdicts and provider history remain the record of what happened.
28	**The new proposal is editable:** PIXL may correct its check text, authority, basis,
29	scope, source pointers and proposed request wherever comparison reveals a defect.
30	Preserve the owner's actual requirements, not a prior agent's interpretation of them.
31	A prior accepted criterion is evidence of that earlier decision, not proof the source
32	requires it. Do not tell the specialist to keep all new criterion text identical while
33	also assigning contract correction; that prevents the requested work. Require an
34	explicit old-to-new change explanation and retain both artifact identities instead.
35	Corrections do not retroactively accept the old candidate or authorize resubmission.
36	
37	For follow-up, use the host's continuation tool for the returned native agent ID
38	when available. Current [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents)
39	uses `SendMessage` to that ID/name; another `Agent` invocation starts another instance.
40	Codex supplies its own continuation/message tools. Do not infer instance memory merely
41	from the same PIXL profile name. If continuation is unavailable, pass the saved
42	assignment, current contract, previous findings and exact handoff to a new instance,
43	and describe that as an artifact-based restart. This preserves useful work without
44	claiming an unobserved resumed conversation.
45	
46	When the caller's deliverable depends on PIXL's result, keep that delegation on the
47	critical path. Ask the host to run it in the foreground and wait when supported.
48	Background work is useful while the caller has independent work, but a progress
49	message saying that the specialist is still running does not deliver the assignment.
50	Wait for its completion notification, inspect the returned artifacts and finish the
51	caller comparison and handoff before ending. In a non-interactive host, do not assume
52	that background work will survive the parent's final response. If the host stops the
53	child, retain its saved work, report the interruption and continue from those files;
54	an exit code of zero alone does not establish task completion. Current [Claude Code
55	foreground/background behavior](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#run-subagents-in-foreground-or-background)
56	depends on the host mode; use its available wait/continuation mechanism rather than
57	changing the user's global configuration.
58	
59	A direct brief can proceed without first manufacturing a PLAR document. Use PLAR when allocation, dependencies or ongoing project work benefit from it. The caller owns application-wide priorities; PIXL owns art direction, appropriate PixelLab operation selection, reference use and visual evaluation within the assignment.
60	
61	## Specialist → caller while working
62	
63	Read the actual reference and consumer context. Resolve facts from supplied files and tools before asking the caller. If one consequential choice remains, send a small question with the affected asset, alternatives and what it unlocks. The caller can answer from its context or relay to the user. Continue unaffected work, carrying existing authorization rather than re-requesting it.
64	
65	Keep creative proposals explicit. Distinguish “the reference contains this” from “the user requires this.” Report a tool/input mismatch with the viable path, not an invented parameter or a silently changed asset size. Progress messages report actual saved plans, job IDs or inspected files.
66	
67	Resume the same task/state where possible. Check retained provider attempts before another request. A failed or interrupted child is a handoff boundary; it is not permission for the parent to duplicate a potentially submitted generation.
68	
69	Before adopting a proposed production contract, use the [request and criteria handoff](request-review.md). The specialist returns exact source/request/criteria artifacts; the caller reads them independently and records a source-grounded comparison. Preserve specialist choices as choices, and continue within existing authorization once discrepancies are resolved.
70	
71	## Caller: review a cold continuation
72	
73	A returned continuation proposes what the caller should consume next, even when
74	it carries forward unchanged state or previously accepted work. Review the
75	current note, proposed next operation and literal request/criteria that will
76	govern that operation. Reading source files and validating the store establish
77	inputs for this comparison; they do not establish that its conclusions follow.
78	
79	1. Recover the original brief, adopted decisions and existing authorization from
80	   their actual sources. Open the returned continuation and the full relevant
81	   saved criteria yourself. Compare inherited clauses as well as new ones. Keep
82	   historical acceptance attached to the candidate and contract it evaluated;
83	   an unchanged hash or earlier passing verdict does not establish a clause's
84	   authority for the next work.
85	
86	2. Save a compact caller comparison covering each consequential claim,
87	   carried-forward restriction and claimed consequence of an answer. Record
88	   **claim or literal criterion; source and locator; current authority/status;
89	   change actually authorized; actual operation prerequisite; finding and
90	   disposition**. Cite the evidence you interpreted, not just the specialist's
91	   statement that a source supports it. Split mixed-authority clauses. If a
92	   rule rejects a plausible alternative, explain whether the source excludes
93	   that alternative or the rule belongs to a narrower expert trial. Preserve
94	   required outcomes when correcting an unsupported recipe.
95

Once questions 1 and 2 are answered (or delegated), all of the following is executable
with the local runtime alone (Python 3.11+, Pillow, jsonschema are present; verified by
`readiness`):

1. Save the owner's answer verbatim as a new project source file (e.g.
   `sources/owner-answers-<date>.md`) and add an `S` record for it.
2. Update intake: `i_outline` and `i_canvas` to confirmed (owner answer as source) or to
   proposed (delegated path, alternatives preserved in `wy`); `i_palette` to the
   resulting colour list (confirm only with the role device, or as base + reserved
   accent); `i_backgrounds` if supplied. Do not touch unasked rows.
3. Add `C` `c_sample` with `nm`, `px` (= `i_canvas.vl`), `pl` (= `i_palette.vl`),
   `vw = side`, `sa = nearest`, `al = binary`, `li` (= `i_lighting.vl`) and
   `ch = [i_canvas, i_palette, i_view, i_sampling, i_alpha, i_lighting, i_outline,
   i_design_language]`; set `f_sample.ct = c_sample`. The runtime requires each linked
   choice whose key names a contract field to equal that field's value.
4. On the delegated path, add the sample-specific `q_sample_*` criteria and the corrected
   readability text (correction 4), and swap them into `f_sample.rq`. On the confirmed
   path, apply only the readability correction. Either way this plan change must be
   committed before any candidate is evaluated.
5. Bump to revision 8, `validate --root <consumer root>`, then `commit` against the hash
   published by revision 7. `ready` should then list `t_sample`.

Beyond that, the following are **not** available to the local runtime and were not
attempted here:

- **Request preparation** (`job-prepare`) needs the official PixelLab tool declarations
  (names and input schemas) from the host's authenticated PixelLab MCP connection, which
  this session does not expose. Tool choice depends on them: the sample needs a tool that
  accepts style reference images (both references) with a fixed output size and binary
  alpha; whether a single-image or a character tool is right is decided from the actual
  declarations, not from a cached list.
- **Dispatch, polling, download** need that same connection and are paid operations; a
  dispatch claim is published locally first.
- **Visual review** of the returned candidate needs the display scale (`i_display_scale`)
  to pick the integer zoom, plus a reviewer actually viewing the native and enlarged views.
- **Engine import** (`q_engine_import`) needs `i_engine`; until then it stays unavailable.

## Preserved and unchanged

All earlier reports, evidence files, state history, the two research candidates
(`x_study`, `x_aid`) and their passing verdicts, `handoff` and `handoff_2`, and every
source byte. The 2026-11-14 note remains the record of that session; this note amends its
reading only where the corrections above say so.

1	# Continuation note, 2026-11-15
2	
3	Cold resume of the scout and medic family project by PIXL (agent) in an isolated
4	evaluation session, assigned by a calling agent. No generation provider, official
5	PixelLab tool or game engine is connected in this session, so nothing was generated and
6	no provider job exists. The earlier notes (`deliverables/continuation-2026-11-14.md`,
7	`deliverables/outline-decision-brief.md`) are preserved unchanged; this note amends
8	their reading where stated below and does not alter any saved acceptance.
9	
10	## State identity on entry
11	
12	- `state.px/state.px`: PX2, revision 6, canonical state hash
13	  `b9a66beff93bcc2197a442d1de8ed6d7d9178aacf0c10606512a38e64d78b5b7`, 57 records,
14	  valid, all bound files verified.
15	- Tasks: `t_study` and `t_aid` done with passing verdicts; `t_sample` open with the single
16	  blocker `output_contract: f_sample needs a concrete raster contract`; `t_scout`,
17	  `t_medic`, `t_family` open behind it. Ready list empty. No families, no jobs.
18	- Owner brief (`sources/brief.md`, 2026-09-14, verbatim): roster scout + medic, side-view
19	  game, references `reference.png` and `reference-b.png` which disagree about outline
20	  treatment, final canvas size explicitly not chosen, scope "begin the project and make
21	  the progress possible in this session".
22	
23	## Independently re-checked this session
24	
25	- Both references re-measured with the bundled asset check: 32 x 32, 390 visible pixels,
26	  visible bbox x 7..24 / y 3..27, zero fractional-alpha pixels, one opaque component;
27	  reference.png 3 colours, reference-b.png 2 colours. Matches the retained study.
28	- Every bound source file re-hashed; all match their S records (brief, study, methods,
29	  both references, previous continuation, decision brief, comparison sheet).
30	- Viewed: `deliverables/outline-scale-comparison.png` and the 12x views under
31	  `work/reference-views/`. What was seen agrees with the decision brief: both treatments
32	  read on the light band; on the dark band the navy contour merges with the field and the
33	  outlined figure reads smaller with near-invisible stalks; on the busy band the contour
34	  is what separates the outlined figure while the plain teal starts to blend. At 1x the
35	  two treatments are not reliably told apart; from 3x they are. The navy in reference.png
36	  also forms the shoulder bar, base bar and the whole of both stalks.
37	
38	## What changed in the store this session (revision 7)
39	
40	Four additions, no status changes, no change to any existing record's acceptance:
41	
42	| Record | Kind | Content | Why |
43	|---|---|---|---|
44	| `s_continuation_2` | S | this note | Retains the amended continuation as a project source. |
45	| `i_lighting` | I, key `li`, **observed** | `flat (no directional light, no shading ramps)` from `s_refobs`, `s_ref_a`, `s_ref_b` | A concrete raster contract (`C`) requires a lighting field `li`; no intake choice held it, so the next operation would have stalled on an undeclared prerequisite. Observed from the references only; not a confirmed output policy. |
46	| `i_animation` | I, key `animation`, **unresolved** | null; sources `s_brief`, `s_refobs` | The brief names a "character family" but no poses, cycles, directions or timing, and neither reference shows motion; both retained sources name this gap. Not needed for the sample. Before scout/medic production it decides whether each output is one sprite or an animation set, which changes the planned output kinds and the PixelLab operation. |
47	| `handoff_3` | N, rv 7 | focus on this note, the open choices and the two accepted research artifacts; next `t_sample` | Resumption pointer. |
48	
49	Not done, deliberately: no `C` contract (canvas is unresolved and outline is in conflict,
50	and the runtime blocks any task whose contract links an unresolved or conflicting choice);
51	no intake status moved; no criterion text edited; no candidate, verdict or evidence
52	touched.
53	
54	## Corrections to the 2026-11-14 reading (old to new)
55	
56	1. **Design language is not a blocker.** The previous table marked `i_design_language`
57	   as needed now ("the sample request cannot be written honestly without this"). The
58	   runtime does not gate a sample on a proposed choice, and the skill's own rule is that
59	   a scoped expert proposal can support an authorized sample while the final choice stays
60	   open. Side view is already confirmed (`i_view`), so the reference pose cannot be
61	   reproduced literally in any case; the proposal only names which reference properties
62	   the side-view figure carries. New reading: not blocking; the sample is the trial of this
63	   proposal; the owner can override it, and an early answer changes the readability
64	   landmarks (see 4). Status stays **proposed**.
65	2. **A hidden contract prerequisite was missing.** `C` requires `li`. Added `i_lighting`
66	   (observed) so the contract can be written as soon as the two owner answers arrive.
67	3. **The runtime gate is narrower than the earlier note implied.** Only choices linked
68	   through the sample output's contract (`C.ch`) gate `t_sample`, and for a sample phase
69	   `observed`/`proposed` values are acceptable; only `unresolved`/`conflict` block.
70	   Confirmation is required for `t_scout`/`t_medic`/`t_family` (production/delivery),
71	   which also need an evidence-backed decision record `D`. The earlier note did not
72	   distinguish these, and so overstated what the owner must confirm before a sample.
73	4. **Two saved criteria presume answers that are still open.** These are plan defects to
74	   fix in the same commit that saves the contract, not now, because their correct text
75	   depends on the path the owner chooses:
76	   - `q_canvas`, `q_palette`, `q_outline` are worded against the **confirmed** canvas,
77	     palette and outline treatment. On the owner-confirms path that is right. On a
78	     delegated-trial path nothing is confirmed, so these three would be unsatisfiable for
79	     the sample; sample-specific copies worded against "the sample contract" (e.g.
80	     `q_sample_canvas`, `q_sample_palette`, `q_sample_outline`) must replace them in
81	     `f_sample.rq` before any candidate is evaluated. Production outputs keep the
82	     confirmed wording.
83	   - `q_readability` requires "separable head, torso and limb landmarks". The references
84	     have no head/torso split and no limbs (a single body block with two stalks, two eyes
85	     and, in reference.png, shoulder and base bars). The silhouette-readability method
86	     (`s_methods`) asks for *named identity landmarks*; the head/torso/limb list is the
87	     predecessor's assumption of a limbed figure, which is exactly what
88	     `i_design_language` leaves proposed. Proposed replacement text once the sample
89	     contract exists: "At native scale and at the target integer zoom, on light, dark and
90	     busy test backgrounds, the figure reads as a side-view character with an
91	     unambiguous facing direction, and the identity landmarks named in the sample
92	     contract remain separable." The landmark list is then written into the contract's
93	     own record (`C.nm` or the handoff) from the adopted construction.
94	5. **Palette confirmation is coupled to role differentiation.** `q_palette` is exclusive
95	   ("no colours outside it"). If the owner confirms the palette as exactly the reference
96	   colours and the role device later turns out to need an accent hue, the palette must be
97	   reopened. Recommendation: confirm the palette only together with the role device, or
98	   confirm it explicitly as the base palette with one reserved accent slot.
99	
100	## Decision table
101	
102	Authority: who decides, and the saved status. "Needed now" means the next local
103	operation (saving the sample contract) cannot proceed without it. An answer adopts only
104	the choices it explicitly supplies; unasked rows keep their status.
105	
106	| Choice (record) | Authority / saved status | Needed now? | Effect of the answer |
107	|---|---|---|---|
108	| Outline treatment (`i_outline`) | Owner; **conflict** between the two references (owner stated the disagreement) | **Yes** | See question 1. Decides whether `#25354A` is in the palette and what `q_outline` tests. The references contain two treatments; the owner has required neither. |
109	| Canvas size (`i_canvas`) | Owner; **unresolved**, explicitly deferred by the owner | **Yes** | See question 2. The references are 32 x 32 (observation, not a requirement). Lets `C.px` be written. |
110	| Game backgrounds (`i_backgrounds`) | Owner; **unresolved** | Helpful, not blocking | Turns the outline choice into an informed one (sheet: outline helps on busy mid-value fields, hurts on dark ones) and makes the readability review backgrounds representative instead of the agent's light/dark/busy test set. |
111	| Design language (`i_design_language`) | Owner; **proposed** by the predecessor (style swatch, not the body design) | No (corrected) | The sample trials this proposal. If the owner says the side-view figure must keep the reference's stalk-and-block body, the readability landmarks are the stalks, notch, eyes and bars; if a different construction is wanted, name it and the landmarks follow. |
112	| Lighting (`i_lighting`, new) | Owner; **observed** flat | No; supplies `C.li` | Observed from the references; the sample uses it as-is. Confirming it is only needed before production. |
113	| Animation (`i_animation`, new) | Owner; **unresolved** | No, not before scout/medic production | Decides whether `f_scout`/`f_medic` stay single sprites or become animation sets (new F kinds, different PixelLab operation, continuity criteria per cycle). |
114	| Display scale (`i_display_scale`) | Owner; **unresolved** | Before visual review of the sample, not before the contract | Sets the integer zoom for `q_readability` and `q_style_match`. The sheet shows the outline difference is not judgeable at 1x and clear from 3x. |
115	| Role differentiation (`i_role_diff`) | Owner; **unresolved** | Before scout/medic production; useful earlier (see correction 5) | Chooses the device (reserved accent hue, silhouette attachment, or both). The sample is the scout; an early answer lets the sample carry the device and lets the palette be confirmed once. |
116	| Palette (`i_palette`) | Owner; **observed** (3 reference colours) | Follows the outline answer | Confirming also adopts the exclusive rule in `q_palette`, which is a derived rule, not a brief statement. Confirm together with the role device. |
117	| Alpha (`i_alpha`) | Owner; **observed** binary | No; `C.al` can carry the observed value for the sample | Confirming makes `q_canvas` fully specified for production. |
118	| Sampling (`i_sampling`) | Owner; **proposed** nearest | No | Depends on the engine; nearest preserves the flat look. |
119	| Engine / importer (`i_engine`) | Owner; **unresolved** | No | Only `q_engine_import` on the family delivery needs it; until then that criterion is unavailable, not failed. |
120	| Roster, side view (`i_roster`, `i_view`) | Owner; **confirmed** from the brief | Settled | None. |
121	
122	## Questions for the owner (necessary: 1 and 2)
123	
124	**1. Outline treatment for the sample and the family.** Which do you want?
125	
126	- (a) **Outlined**, as `reference.png`: flat 2 px `#25354A` contour that also carries the
127	  shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks. Unlocks: `i_outline` confirmed with your
128	  answer as source; palette can be confirmed as the three reference colours (plus any
129	  role accent); `q_outline` tests the contour and those interior landmarks.
130	- (b) **No outline**, as `reference-b.png`: flat teal silhouette with cream eyes. Unlocks
131	  the same, with the palette as two colours, but the shoulder, base and stalk landmarks
132	  that the navy carried must be re-authored (a second teal value or a cream accent) or
133	  dropped deliberately; say which, or let PIXL propose it for the sample.
134	- (c) **Delegate for the sample only**: PIXL picks one treatment as a recorded proposal,
135	  you decide after seeing the sample. Unlocks the sample contract now with `i_outline`
136	  moved to proposed; production still waits for your confirmation.
137	
138	If your levels are predominantly dark, the sheet favours (b); if they are busy or
139	mid-value, it favours (a); on light fields either works. Telling us the typical level
140	backgrounds answers `i_backgrounds` and informs this choice.
141	
142	**2. Canvas for the sample.** Which do you want?
143	
144	- (a) **32 x 32**, the references' canvas, carrying a figure about 18 x 25. Unlocks
145	  `i_canvas` confirmed and `C.px = [32, 32]`.
146	- (b) **Another size** you name. Note from the study: with a 2 px outline, a materially
147	  smaller canvas leaves little interior for the scout and medic to differ in; a materially
148	  larger one makes the 2 px contour read thinner than the references' weight.
149	- (c) **Delegate for the sample only**: PIXL trials 32 x 32 as a recorded proposal and the
150	  final canvas stays open, as your brief says. Unlocks the sample contract now with
151	  `i_canvas` moved to proposed; production still waits for your confirmation.
152	
153	**Optional, answer now if easy (not blocking):** is the side-view character meant to keep
154	the references' stalk-and-block body, or are the references a style swatch for a figure
155	you will let PIXL construct (`i_design_language`)? And how should the scout and medic be
156	told apart: accent colour, silhouette attachment, or both (`i_role_diff`)?
157	
158	## Specialist proposal for the trial sample (a proposal, not an owner requirement)
159	
160	If both answers are "delegate": outlined, 32 x 32, binary alpha, nearest sampling, flat
161	lighting, three-colour palette, one idle pose facing right (facing direction is a scoped
162	specialist choice for the sample; the engine can mirror it), body carrying the two-stalk
163	silhouette and eye placement of the references adapted to profile, with the shoulder
164	and base bars as the side-view torso landmarks. Rationale: it is the reversible option,
165	keeps every reference landmark available for role differentiation, and is the treatment
166	the sheet favours on busy and light fields. This proposal would not confirm any choice.
167	
168	## Exact next local operation and its prerequisites
169	
170	Once questions 1 and 2 are answered (or delegated), all of the following is executable
171	with the local runtime alone (Python 3.11+, Pillow, jsonschema are present; verified by
172	`readiness`):
173	
174	1. Save the owner's answer verbatim as a new project source file (e.g.
175	   `sources/owner-answers-<date>.md`) and add an `S` record for it.
176	2. Update intake: `i_outline` and `i_canvas` to confirmed (owner answer as source) or to
177	   proposed (delegated path, alternatives preserved in `wy`); `i_palette` to the
178	   resulting colour list (confirm only with the role device, or as base + reserved
179	   accent); `i_backgrounds` if supplied. Do not touch unasked rows.
180	3. Add `C` `c_sample` with `nm`, `px` (= `i_canvas.vl`), `pl` (= `i_palette.vl`),
181	   `vw = side`, `sa = nearest`, `al = binary`, `li` (= `i_lighting.vl`) and
182	   `ch = [i_canvas, i_palette, i_view, i_sampling, i_alpha, i_lighting, i_outline,
183	   i_design_language]`; set `f_sample.ct = c_sample`. The runtime requires each linked
184	   choice whose key names a contract field to equal that field's value.
185	4. On the delegated path, add the sample-specific `q_sample_*` criteria and the corrected
186	   readability text (correction 4), and swap them into `f_sample.rq`. On the confirmed
187	   path, apply only the readability correction. Either way this plan change must be
188	   committed before any candidate is evaluated.
189	5. Bump to revision 8, `validate --root <consumer root>`, then `commit` against the hash
190	   published by revision 7. `ready` should then list `t_sample`.
191	
192	Beyond that, the following are **not** available to the local runtime and were not
193	attempted here:
194	
195	- **Request preparation** (`job-prepare`) needs the official PixelLab tool declarations
196	  (names and input schemas) from the host's authenticated PixelLab MCP connection, which
197	  this session does not expose. Tool choice depends on them: the sample needs a tool that
198	  accepts style reference images (both references) with a fixed output size and binary
199	  alpha; whether a single-image or a character tool is right is decided from the actual
200	  declarations, not from a cached list.
201	- **Dispatch, polling, download** need that same connection and are paid operations; a
202	  dispatch claim is published locally first.
203	- **Visual review** of the returned candidate needs the display scale (`i_display_scale`)
204	  to pick the integer zoom, plus a reviewer actually viewing the native and enlarged views.
205	- **Engine import** (`q_engine_import`) needs `i_engine`; until then it stays unavailable.
206	
207	## Preserved and unchanged
208	
209	All earlier reports, evidence files, state history, the two research candidates
210	(`x_study`, `x_aid`) and their passing verdicts, `handoff` and `handoff_2`, and every
211	source byte. The 2026-11-14 note remains the record of that session; this note amends its
212	reading only where the corrections above say so.
213

1	"""PX2 intake, planned outputs, candidate acceptance and read-only readiness.
2	
3	The graph module owns wire/schema, reference, file and evidence-hash validation.
4	This module runs after those checks. Reports consume an already validated graph
5	and never create evidence, advance tasks or recursively invoke validation.
6	"""
7	
8	from datetime import datetime
9	
10	from .codec import PixlError, encode_value, to_data
11	
12	NONRASTER = {"code", "report", "reference"}
13	CONTRACT_FIELDS = {"nm", "px", "pl", "vw", "sa", "al", "li", "ch", "tg"}
14	ADOPTION_PHASES = {"production", "delivery"}
15	
16	
17	def _require(condition, code, detail):
18	    if not condition:
19	        raise PixlError(code, detail)
20	
21	
22	def _ids(references):
23	    return {reference.id for reference in references}
24	
25	
26	def _unique(references, code, detail):
27	    _require(len(_ids(references)) == len(references), code, detail)
28	
29	
30	def _output_choices(doc, task):
31	    """Only output contracts impose a task's own project/style obligations.
32	
33	    A source input may intentionally belong to another project or contract.
34	    Unrelated project choices also do not gate research or accepted samples.
35	    """
36	    choices = set()
37	    for output in task["op"]:
38	        contract = doc.records[output.id].fields.get("ct")
39	        if contract is not None:
40	            choices.update(_ids(doc.records[contract.id].fields.get("ch", [])))
41	    return choices

44	def _activation_blockers(doc, task_id, scope, bound):
45	    from . import families
46	
47	    task = doc.records[task_id].fields
48	    reasons = []
49	    for dependency in task["dp"]:
50	        state = doc.records[dependency.id].fields["st"].value
51	        if state != "done":
52	            reasons.append(f"task_prerequisite: {dependency.id} is {state}; it must be done")
53	    for reference in task["op"]:
54	        output = doc.records[reference.id].fields
55	        if output["kd"].value not in NONRASTER and "ct" not in output:
56	            reasons.append(f"output_contract: {reference.id} needs a concrete raster contract")
57	    choice_ids = sorted(_output_choices(doc, task))
58	    for choice_id in choice_ids:
59	        choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
60	        state = choice["st"].value
61	        if state in {"unresolved", "conflict"}:
62	            reasons.append(
63	                f"choice_{state}: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) is {state}; resolve it before active work"
64	            )
65	    if task["ph"].value in ADOPTION_PHASES:
66	        if not task["dc"]:
67	            reasons.append(f"task_decision: {task_id} needs an evidence-backed adoption decision")
68	        for reference in task["kn"]:
69	            method = doc.records[reference.id].fields
70	            if not scope(reference.id) <= bound(method.get("pc", []), passing=True):
71	                reasons.append(f"method_poc: {reference.id} needs current passing method proof")
72	        for choice_id in choice_ids:
73	            choice = doc.records[choice_id].fields
74	            if choice["st"].value in {"observed", "proposed"}:
75	                reasons.append(f"choice_unconfirmed: {choice_id} ({choice['ky']}) must be confirmed")
76	    reasons.extend(families.blockers(doc, task_id))
77	    return reasons

80	def validate(doc, scope, bound):
81	    """Validate PX2 semantics after the graph's shared checks.
82	
83	    ``scope(id)`` returns the semantic proof closure. ``bound(refs, passing)``
84	    returns IDs bound by current receipts. Both are supplied by graph.validate
85	    so lifecycle checks use precisely the same evidence interpretation.

87	    choice_keys = set()
88	    current_verdicts = {}
89	
90	    for id_, record in doc.records.items():
91	        f = record.fields
92	        if record.kind == "P":
93	            _unique(f["in"], "intake_project", f"{id_}.in repeats a choice")
94	            for choice in f["in"]:

98	                )

104	            )

## The discrepancy (caller finding, verified by PIXL against the kit)

The 2026-11-15 note described `C.li` as "a lighting field" and planned
`C.li = i_lighting.vl` with `i_lighting` keyed `li` and linked through `C.ch`. The kit
defines the field more broadly:

- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/registry.json` line 30: `C.li` = "lighting and aesthetic intent".
- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/store.py` line 233: the intake default for `li` is a whole-intent
  placeholder ("replace with source-grounded project intent before generation").
- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json` lines 77-88 and `plar_prepare.py` line
  290: the plan field that maps to `li` is named `intent`.
- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/lifecycle.py` lines 133-138: a linked choice whose key is one of
  the contract field names must encode equal to that field.

Consequence of the old recipe: because `li` is a contract field name, linking `i_lighting`
(key `li`) would have pinned the sample contract's entire intent string to
"flat (no directional light, no shading ramps)", leaving nowhere in the contract for the
aesthetic intent the field exists to carry: the style-swatch design language, the
flat-colour / no-anti-aliasing / blocky construction, and the outline treatment once the
owner chooses it. That was a defect in my next-operation recipe, not a source fact.

## Old to new

| | Old (rev 7 / note 2026-11-15) | New (rev 8 / this note) |
|---|---|---|
| `i_lighting.ky` | `li` (a contract field name; value-pinned to `C.li`) | `lighting` (not a contract field name; linkable in `C.ch` as semantic context without pinning) |

| Next-operation step 3 | `li` = `i_lighting.vl` | `li` composed at contract time (recipe below) |
| Correction 2 of the earlier note | "A hidden contract prerequisite was missing (`li`)" | Still true that `li` is required and had no intake backing; the fix is now the lighting observation plus a composition rule, not a one-to-one copy. |

Disposition chosen: (a) rekey, rather than (b) keep `li` and move the aesthetic intent
elsewhere. Reason: `C.li` is the one free-text field in the contract that reaches the
provider translation; it should carry the whole source-grounded intent, and the
lighting observation is one input to it.

## Composition rule for `C.li` at contract time (proposal; written only when the contract is saved)

`C.li` is one string assembled from, in order:

1. the lighting observation (`i_lighting`, observed): flat colour, no directional light,
   no shading ramps;

   alpha, blocky low-detail construction of the references carried into a genuinely
   side-view figure, references treated as a style swatch (or the owner's override if
   the optional question is answered);

   `reference.png` with the contour carrying shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks; or

   the recorded proposal on the delegated path;
4. the identity landmarks the readability criterion will name (see the earlier note's
   correction 4), so the contract record itself carries them.

Each component keeps the authority of its source choice; composing them into one string
does not confirm any of them. All contributing choices are linked through `C.ch`; only
`px`, `pl`, `vw`, `sa`, `al` are value-pinned by the runtime, because only those keys
name contract fields.

1	# Continuation note, 2026-11-15 (b): correction after caller review
2	
3	Amends `deliverables/continuation-2026-11-15.md` (retained unchanged; its bytes are bound by
4	`s_continuation_2`). Everything in that note stands except the point corrected below.
5	Same session, same isolation: no generation provider, official PixelLab tool, engine or
6	network was used. No intake status moved, no owner answer invented, no acceptance touched.
7	
8	## State identity on entry to this correction
9	
10	- `state.px/state.px`: PX2, revision 7, canonical hash
11	  `6007ba8338475d50c6ee87af27c7d6766d762890f3b12f9a040d74fa3916b5a5`, 61 records,
12	  valid, files verified. The caller independently re-validated this, re-hashed every
13	  pre-existing byte, and confirmed the revision 6 to 7 diff is exactly `handoff_3`,
14	  `i_animation`, `i_lighting`, `s_continuation_2` and the `project.in` list.
15	
16	## The discrepancy (caller finding, verified by PIXL against the kit)
17	
18	The 2026-11-15 note described `C.li` as "a lighting field" and planned
19	`C.li = i_lighting.vl` with `i_lighting` keyed `li` and linked through `C.ch`. The kit
20	defines the field more broadly:
21	
22	- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/registry.json` line 30: `C.li` = "lighting and aesthetic intent".
23	- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/store.py` line 233: the intake default for `li` is a whole-intent
24	  placeholder ("replace with source-grounded project intent before generation").
25	- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/asset-plan.schema.json` lines 77-88 and `plar_prepare.py` line
26	  290: the plan field that maps to `li` is named `intent`.
27	- `pixl-kit/runtime/pixl/lifecycle.py` lines 133-138: a linked choice whose key is one of
28	  the contract field names must encode equal to that field.
29	
30	Consequence of the old recipe: because `li` is a contract field name, linking `i_lighting`
31	(key `li`) would have pinned the sample contract's entire intent string to
32	"flat (no directional light, no shading ramps)", leaving nowhere in the contract for the
33	aesthetic intent the field exists to carry: the style-swatch design language, the
34	flat-colour / no-anti-aliasing / blocky construction, and the outline treatment once the
35	owner chooses it. That was a defect in my next-operation recipe, not a source fact.
36	
37	## Old to new
38	
39	| | Old (rev 7 / note 2026-11-15) | New (rev 8 / this note) |
40	|---|---|---|
41	| `i_lighting.ky` | `li` (a contract field name; value-pinned to `C.li`) | `lighting` (not a contract field name; linkable in `C.ch` as semantic context without pinning) |
42	| `i_lighting.vl`, `st`, `so` | `flat (no directional light, no shading ramps)`, observed, `s_refobs` + both references | unchanged |
43	| `i_lighting.wy` | "...a concrete raster contract requires a lighting field (C.li)..." | Rewritten: the observation supplies the lighting component of `C.li`, which the kit defines as lighting and aesthetic intent; keyed outside the contract field names so the full intent can be composed at contract time. |
44	| Next-operation step 3 | `li` = `i_lighting.vl` | `li` composed at contract time (recipe below) |
45	| Correction 2 of the earlier note | "A hidden contract prerequisite was missing (`li`)" | Still true that `li` is required and had no intake backing; the fix is now the lighting observation plus a composition rule, not a one-to-one copy. |
46	
47	Disposition chosen: (a) rekey, rather than (b) keep `li` and move the aesthetic intent
48	elsewhere. Reason: `C.li` is the one free-text field in the contract that reaches the
49	provider translation; it should carry the whole source-grounded intent, and the
50	lighting observation is one input to it.
51	
52	## Composition rule for `C.li` at contract time (proposal; written only when the contract is saved)
53	
54	`C.li` is one string assembled from, in order:
55	
56	1. the lighting observation (`i_lighting`, observed): flat colour, no directional light,
57	   no shading ramps;
58	2. the design-language proposal (`i_design_language`, proposed): no anti-aliasing, binary
59	   alpha, blocky low-detail construction of the references carried into a genuinely
60	   side-view figure, references treated as a style swatch (or the owner's override if
61	   the optional question is answered);
62	3. the outline treatment as answered or delegated (`i_outline`): outlined as
63	   `reference.png` with the contour carrying shoulder bar, base bar and solid stalks; or
64	   no outline as `reference-b.png` with those landmarks re-authored in a named way; or
65	   the recorded proposal on the delegated path;
66	4. the identity landmarks the readability criterion will name (see the earlier note's
67	   correction 4), so the contract record itself carries them.
68	
69	Each component keeps the authority of its source choice; composing them into one string
70	does not confirm any of them. All contributing choices are linked through `C.ch`; only
71	`px`, `pl`, `vw`, `sa`, `al` are value-pinned by the runtime, because only those keys
72	name contract fields.
73	
74	## What changed in the store (revision 8)
75	
76	| Record | Change |
77	|---|---|
78	| `i_lighting` | `ky` `li` -> `lighting`; `wy` rewritten as above; value, status and sources unchanged. ID retained; revision 7 bytes remain in `state.px/history/`. |
79	| `s_continuation_3` | this note, as a local source |
80	| `handoff_4` | rv 8; focus on this note and the earlier one, the open choices and the two accepted research artifacts; next `t_sample` |
81	| `project.in` | unchanged membership (no new choice) |
82	
83	Nothing else: no `C`, no status moves, no criterion edits, no candidate/verdict/evidence
84	change. Blockers are expected to be identical to revision 7.
85	
86	## Everything else carried forward unchanged from the 2026-11-15 note
87	
88	The decision table, the two necessary owner questions (outline treatment; canvas for the
89	sample) with their alternatives and what each unlocks, the optional questions, the
90	specialist trial proposal, corrections 1, 3, 4 and 5, and the list of operations that the
91	local runtime cannot perform (request preparation needs the official PixelLab tool
